name: Your Bird Can Sing
_note: ADDED 2026-09-22 from Daniel's brief, with the signet-new-act skill. His words: a multi-instrumental duo, a playful sing-along celebration of the Beatles, fit for kids through seniors, marketed into senior living among other places but not only there. No site, no channel, no photographs and no footage yet, so the page carries original artwork instead (scripts/bird_art.py) and the footage gap is open. Everything on the page traces either to his brief or to the site's own repertoire page, which already publishes eleven Beatles songs with Hey Jude and Let It Be flagged singalong.
_presentation_note: SPEC'D ON DANIEL'S RULING 2026-09-22: 'publish under the act name. no additional names.' The act has a proper name and is booked by it, so `name` is what publishes and no person is named anywhere, the same shape as Firstwater and Last Consulate. He also ruled the instruments out the same day ('this doesn't matter don't include it'), so `spec` carries the fact he did give, that it is a multi-instrumental duo, rather than the instrument list a spec line usually carries. It sits in the roster intro's named-acts sentence for the reason Firstwater does: the specific act comes with the booking. 2026-09-24: 'multi-instrumental' left the published spec line on the fifth pass, because with no instrument named it tells a buyer nothing; it remains his fact here.
_label_note: URL AND LABELS ON DANIEL'S RULING 2026-09-22: 'beatles-sing-along, it's not a cover band or impersonation or tribute.' Autocomplete the same day had 'beatles tribute band denver' and 'beatles cover band denver' as the top completions for their stems, and both were rejected as untrue of this act: no costumes, no impersonation, and a duo is not a band. The page therefore reaches buyers on 'beatles sing-along', 'beatles music' and the sing-along family that does describe it ('sing along songs for seniors', 'sing along music for seniors', 'beatles sing along songs', all completing 2026-09-22), and carries no word it would have to take back. Search terms lose to the truth here; act-labels-are-search-terms is a rule about which true word to pick, not a licence to pick a false one.
spec: A Beatles sing-along led by two musicians, for everyone from five to ninety
byline_inline: a Beatles sing-along led by two musicians, for everyone from five to ninety
_bucket_note: Specialty only. It is the set piece a crowd takes part in, which is what that bucket means. Party was left off because there is no dance floor, cocktail because nobody talks over a sing-along, and budget because that tag is a claim reserved for solo acts.
_config_note: One size, on his call 2026-09-22: 'for now it's a duo.' One configuration means no ladder section on the page, the same call Firstwater's entry records: a one-row table shows nothing.
_genre_note: The two existing genres the catalogue sits in. No Beatles genre was minted: one act does not make a filter row, and the label a buyer would pick from a list is the era, not the band.
_img_note: Original artwork, not a photograph and not an interim still: a flock in silhouette flying into a sunburst, drawn from scratch in scripts/bird_art.py in the visual language of mid-sixties sleeve design. Daniel asked for Beatles cover art on the page (2026-09-22) and then set the terms himself: published album covers are copyrighted artwork, so none was used and nothing is reproduced. Rebuild with `python3 scripts/bird_art.py`. One more piece sits on the page, the booklet illustration in the program section; the square sleeve (img/acts/your-bird-can-sing-sleeve.jpg) keeps its provenance row but came off the page 2026-09-24, when the section that explained its own provenance to the buyer was cut. When a photograph of the duo arrives it goes through scripts/act_media.py photo --card and the artwork moves down the page rather than off it.
alt: A flock of birds in silhouette flying into a sunburst, drawn in the flat color of a sixties record sleeve.
blurb: You know the part of Hey Jude where everyone starts singing. A Beatles sing-along is a playful hour of that. Two musicians play and lead the singing, and by the second song that's your whole crowd. It books for family parties, company events, weddings, community programs and senior living, indoors or out.
_identity_note: Fifth pass 2026-09-24 on Daniel's ruling that the booklets are an ops detail for the FAQ, not a feature, and that decibel figures misread the buyer. The feature is two musicians getting a whole crowd singing; the page says that and who books it, and the FAQ carries the how. Two paragraphs, matching the page hero. No instrument is named, per his ruling.
identity: You know the part of Hey Jude where everyone starts singing. A Beatles sing-along is a playful hour of that. Two musicians play and lead the singing, and by the second song that's your whole crowd.

It books for a fiftieth anniversary or an eightieth birthday, a company picnic or holiday party, a wedding welcome party, a school or library program, and an afternoon at a senior living community. Every crowd in that list already knows these songs.
_occasion_note: Four occasions on Daniel's ruling 2026-09-24 ('this is WAY too focused on senior living. that is ONE potential client'): company picnics and holiday parties, wedding welcome parties and after-parties, family parties and daytime programs are all bookings for a sing-along, so the roster filter shows it under each. Senior living is one lane among them.
